current_example.title: Example: Using Properties of Indicator Functions

q-172706.name: Question 1
q-172706.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14188486/assets/b2919328788c6762d1a0b56225b95749e88973ec84803584be0d336f63033566.png)

Which of the following is the subset $A$ of $U=\{a,b,c,d,e\}$ whose indicator function ${1}_{A}(x)$ is shown above?
q-172706.worked_solution:
An indicator function maps elements from a set to the values $0$ or $1,$ depending on whether the element belongs to a specified subset. The indicator function is designed to "indicate" whether an element is a member of a subset.

More specifically, consider a universal set $X.$ Then, the indicator function of a set $A⊆X$ is the function

$$
{1}_{A}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1, & \text{if }x\in A, \\ 0, & \text{if }x\notin A.\end{aligned}
$$

In the diagram above, only the elements $a,b,$ and $d$ are mapped to $1.$ Therefore, the indicator function in the diagram above corresponds to the set $A=\{a,b,d\}.$

q-174359.name: Question 5
q-174359.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14188486/assets/7c60072882a6effae61da543bfddff1053ab0bcc924d12c49f5acd697b0871c4.png)

Which of the following is the subset $A$ of $U=\{a,b,c,d,e\}$ whose indicator function ${1}_{A}(x)$ is shown above?
q-174359.worked_solution:
An indicator function maps elements from a set to the values $0$ or $1,$ depending on whether the element belongs to a specified subset. The indicator function is designed to "indicate" whether an element is a member of a subset.

More specifically, consider a universal set $X.$ Then, the indicator function of a set $A⊆X$ is the function

$$
{1}_{A}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1, & \text{if }x\in A, \\ 0, & \text{if }x\notin A.\end{aligned}
$$

In the diagram above, only the elements $b,c$ and $e$ are mapped to $1.$ Therefore, the indicator function in the diagram above corresponds to the set $A=\{b,c,e\}.$

q-174396.name: Question 6
q-174396.problem:
$$
{1}_{A}(r)=0,\,{1}_{B}(r)=0
$$

Given the values of the indicator functions of the sets $A$ and $B,$ which of the following statements are true?

I. ${1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(r)=1$

II. ${1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(r)=0$

III. $r\in A\cap B$
q-174396.worked_solution:
Recall that the indicator functions of $\overset{―}{A},$ $A\cap B,$ and $A\cup B$ have the following properties:

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{\overset{―}{A}}\,(x) & =1-{1}_{A}(x) \\ {1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(x) & =min\{{1}_{A}(x),{1}_{B}(x)\} \\ {1}_{A\,\cup \,B}\,(x) & =max\{{1}_{A}(x),{1}_{B}(x)\}\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is false while statement II is true. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(r) & =min\{{1}_{A}(r),{1}_{B}(r)\} \\  & =min\{0,0\} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is false. Since ${1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(r)=0,$ we conclude that $r$ does not belong to $A\cap B.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

$$

$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true while statement II is false. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{\overset{―}{A}}\,(0) & =1-{1}_{A}(0) \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
